summary: Milo sits on a low crate in the lower deck of the tanker, struggling to thread a thick copper wire through a series of ceramic insulators while the floor vibrates from a distant sandstorm. Lucia stands over him, her hand resting on the hilt of a ceramic blade tucked into her belt as she watches his grease-stained fingers fumble with the delicate electronics. She leans down and purposefully kicks a small box of essential mounting brackets under a heavy coolant tank, her eyes remaining fixed on Milo to see if he notices the deliberate movement. Milo pauses, his brow furrowing as he looks around the cluttered floor for the missing components, unaware that Lucia has already replaced them with unstable, high-velocity ignition caps. Lucia smiles thinly, her expression hidden in the shadows of the engine room as she watches him reach for the compromised hardware. "The parts you're looking for won't help you build a radio, but they'll certainly make that bird fly faster."

summary: Arvin stands at the base of a towering, patchwork rocket made of corrugated iron and scavenged turbine blades, his hand pressed firmly against the vibrating hull. Milo crouches near the ignition lead, his hands trembling as he prepares to touch the live wires together while the wind howls across the cracked surface of the dry lake bed. The sun hangs low on the horizon, painting the scene in deep oranges and long, dramatic shadows that stretch toward the dust clouds of approaching Aegis interceptors. Arvin nods slowly, his eyes locked on Milo, signaling the start of a countdown that relies more on physical instinct than any digital clock. Milo grips the copper leads, his knuckles white, waiting for the precise moment the pressure gauge hits the red line marked in permanent marker. "Let it go now, before the heat of the core fuses your fingers to the frame."
settingText: The Nomadic Fleet of weathered, maintained tankers.
